newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank Hapoalim issue raises $200 mln.
newsitem.headline: Bank Hapoalim issue raises $200 mln.

text.p: Israel's Bank Hapoalim announced on Wednesday it had raised $200 million in an offering of guaranteed floating rate notes (FRN), which were listed on the London exchange.
Israel's largest commercial bank said the issue, conducted through its subsidiary Hapoalim International, was successful and closed two months ahead of schedule.
"The goal of the offering is to widen Bank Hapoalim's activities in Israel and abroad and to raise long-term sources of foreign currency," it said in a statement.

The bonds, which carry a Moody's A3 rating, offer a one-eighth point premium on Libor for six months. The bonds' final redemption date is July 2006 but bondholders have an option for early redemption in July 2002.
